rules.title: Source-of-income and government-subsidy screening limits (fair housing)
rules.requirement: Housing providers may not discriminate based on source of income, which includes public assistance and housing subsidies such as Section 8 vouchers. Where a government rent subsidy applies, the provider must assess income only against the portion of rent the tenant pays. If the provider uses credit history, the applicant must be offered the option to give alternative evidence of ability to pay. The provider must give reasonable time to respond and reasonably consider that evidence in place of credit history. Providers may still verify employment, request landlord references and verify identity.

coverage.summary: Applies to housing providers renting housing accommodations in California; no unit-count or construction-date limits stated in the passages.

rules.quoted_span: (A) Use a financial or income standard in assessing eligibility for the rental of housing that is not based on the portion of the rent to be paid by the tenant.
rules.review_note: The passages do not show the section number; Gov. Code § 12955 is the likely statute. Effective date is not stated in the passages.
rules.source_notes: Corroborated by the CRD FAQ (D016), which says refusing to rent based on source of income, including Section 8 vouchers, is prohibited.

rules.title: Criminal history screening limits (Civil Rights Council regulations)
rules.requirement: Housing providers may check criminal history but may not consider arrests that did not lead to a conviction, sealed or expunged records, or juvenile justice records. Blanket bans on applicants with a criminal history are prohibited. A denial based on a conviction must be directly related to the applicant's ability to be a good tenant and not a threat to the health and safety of others or the property. The provider should consider the nature and severity of the crime and the time elapsed.

coverage.summary: Applies to housing providers in California; no unit-count or construction-date limits stated in the passages.

rules.effective_date_note: The Jan. 1, 2020 date comes from the secondary source DX07, which says the regulations took effect then.
rules.citation: Cal. Civil Rights Council criminal history regulations (Cal. Code Regs. tit. 2)
citation_aliases: Fair Employment and Housing Council criminal history regulations
rules.quoted_span: Housing providers are also prohibited from having “blanket bans” of all people with a criminal history.
rules.review_note: The passages describe the rule only through a CRD FAQ and a CAA article and give no section number. The primary citation is therefore general.
rules.source_notes: The official source is the CRD FAQ (D016). DX07 (CAA) says the regulations took effect Jan. 1, 2020 and prohibit blanket bans and policies that consider arrests without convictions.
